say.en: Water's organic cousins. Replace one hydrogen of water with an alkyl group and you get an alcohol; with a benzene ring, a phenol; replace both hydrogens and you get an ether. Sanitiser, Dettol and the anaesthetic ether all belong to this family. In this lesson: Classify alcohols, phenols and ethers.

body.en: Alcohols and phenols are mono-, di- or trihydric by the number of –OH groups. When –OH is on an $sp^3$ carbon: primary, secondary or tertiary alcohols, plus allylic and benzylic alcohols. When –OH is on an $sp^2$ carbon: vinylic alcohols and phenols ($C_6H_5OH$). Ethers $R-O-R'$ are simple (symmetrical) when both groups are the same and mixed (unsymmetrical) when they differ.
body.kn: sp³ ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಮೇಲಿನ OH ಆಲ್ಕೋಹಾಲ್: ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ, ದ್ವಿತೀಯಕ ಅಥವಾ ತೃತೀಯಕ. ಬೆಂಜೀನ್ ವಲಯದ ಮೇಲಿನ OH ಫೀನಾಲ್. ಈಥರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಆಕ್ಸಿಜನ್ ಎರಡು ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಗುಂಪುಗಳನ್ನು ಜೋಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಒಂದೇ ಗುಂಪುಗಳಾದರೆ ಸರಳ, ಬೇರೆಯಾದರೆ ಮಿಶ್ರ ಈಥರ್.

title.en: Where the OH sits, and its shape

say.en: Where the OH group sits decides the family: on an sp three carbon it is an alcohol, on a ring carbon it is a phenol.
Alcohols are primary, secondary or tertiary by the carbon that holds the OH.
IUPAC names replace the final e of the alkane by ol, with a number for the position.
In methanol, oxygen is sp three with two lone pairs. They push the bonds together, so the C–O–H angle is 108.9 degrees, a little below tetrahedral.
In phenol the C–O bond is shorter, because the oxygen lone pair is shared with the ring. In ethers the bulky groups open the angle to 111.7 degrees.
Where the OH sits, and its shape.

body.en: Alcohols: replace the final ‘e’ of the alkane by ‘ol’ and number from the end nearer –OH: $CH_3CH(OH)CH_3$ is propan-2-ol; $HOCH_2CH_2OH$ is ethane-1,2-diol; glycerol is propane-1,2,3-triol. Phenols: methylphenols are cresols; benzenediols are catechol (1,2), resorcinol (1,3) and quinol (1,4). Ethers are named as alkoxyalkanes, the larger group being the parent: $C_2H_5OCH_3$ is methoxyethane; $C_6H_5OCH_3$ is methoxybenzene (anisole).

body.en: *Oxygen* is $sp^3$ hybridised with two lone pairs. In methanol the C–O–H angle is 108.9°, slightly less than tetrahedral (lone-pair repulsion). In phenol the C–O bond is 136 pm against 142 pm in methanol: resonance gives it partial double-bond character and the ring carbon is $sp^2$. In methoxymethane the C–O–C angle is 111.7°, opened by the repulsion of the two bulky methyl groups.
body.kn: ಆಕ್ಸಿಜನ್ sp³ ಸಂಕರಣ, ಎರಡು ಏಕಾಂಗಿ ಜೋಡಿಗಳು. ಮೆಥನಾಲ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ C–O–H ಕೋನ 108.9°, ಈಥರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ C–O–C ಕೋನ 111.7°. ಫೀನಾಲ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಅನುರಣನದಿಂದ C–O ಬಂಧ ಚಿಕ್ಕದು.

myth.en: Hydration of propene with dilute H₂SO₄ gives propan-1-ol.

truth.en: Acid-catalysed hydration gives propan-2-ol (Markovnikov). Propan-1-ol needs hydroboration–oxidation. With acid, H⁺ adds first to make the more stable secondary carbocation, so OH ends up on C2. In hydroboration, boron (not H⁺) goes to the end carbon, and it is later replaced by OH.

say.en: Alcohol: –OH on sp³ C; phenol: –OH on a ring carbon; ether: R–O–R′.
Phenol's C–O bond (136 pm) is shorter than methanol's (142 pm); C–O–C in methoxymethane is 111.7°.
Alkene + H₂O/H⁺ → Markovnikov alcohol; hydroboration–oxidation → anti-Markovnikov alcohol.
Grignard + HCHO → 1°, + RCHO → 2°, + ketone → 3° alcohol.
Phenol from Dow's process, sulphonic acid fusion, diazonium salts or cumene (with acetone).

Boron, then OH, goes to the less substituted CH₂ carbon: (CH₃)₂CHCH₂OH, 2-methylpropan-1-ol.

narration.en: Many people think: Hydration of propene with dilute H₂SO₄ gives propan-1-ol. Actually: Acid-catalysed hydration gives propan-2-ol (Markovnikov). Propan-1-ol needs hydroboration–oxidation. With acid, H⁺ adds first to make the more stable secondary carbocation, so OH ends up on C2. In hydroboration, boron (not H⁺) goes to the end carbon, and it is later replaced by OH.

problem.en: Give the IUPAC name and class of: (a) CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃  (b) (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂CH₃  (c) C₆H₅CH₂OH  (d) CH₃OCH₂CH₂CH₃.

steps.en: (a) –OH on C-2 of a four-carbon chain, carbon bonded to two carbons: butan-2-ol, secondary alcohol.
(b) –OH carbon bonded to three carbons: 2-methylbutan-2-ol, tertiary alcohol.
(c) –OH on CH₂ attached to benzene: phenylmethanol (benzyl alcohol), primary benzylic alcohol.
(d) Larger group propane is the parent: 1-methoxypropane, a mixed ether.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Give the IUPAC name and class of: (a) CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃  (b) (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂CH₃  (c) C₆H₅CH₂OH  (d) CH₃OCH₂CH₂CH₃.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Give the IUPAC name and class of: a CH 3CHOHCH 2CH 3 b CH 3 2COHCH 2CH 3 c C 6H 5CH 2OH d CH 3OCH 2CH 2CH 3.
a -OH on C-2 of a four-carbon chain, carbon bonded to two carbons: butan-2-ol, secondary alcohol.
b -OH carbon bonded to three carbons: 2-methylbutan-2-ol, tertiary alcohol.
c -OH on CH 2 attached to benzene: phenylmethanol benzyl alcohol, primary benzylic alcohol.
d Larger group propane is the parent: 1-methoxypropane, a mixed ether.
So the answer is a butan-2-ol, 2 degrees; b 2-methylbutan-2-ol, 3 degrees; c phenylmethanol, 1 degrees benzylic; d 1-methoxypropane, mixed ether.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Calculate the percentage of oxygen by mass in ethane-1,2-diol, HOCH₂CH₂OH (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16).

say.en: Let us solve this together. Calculate the percentage of oxygen by mass in ethane-1,2-diol, HOCH 2CH 2OH (C equals 12, H equals 1, O equals 16).
Formula C 2H 6O 2; molar mass equals 24 plus 6 plus 32 equals 62 grams per mole.
% O equals 32 over 62 times 100 equals 51.6 percent.
So the answer is 51.6 percent oxygen.
